sec: Newer discoveries, diagnostic criteria and pre-diabetes

items.q: In the mnemonic 'Dirty dozen', the letter D is paired with decreased:
items.exp: Under Dirty dozen, D is written as decreased dopamine activity. (Book p919)

items.q: Match the mnemonic letter to the printed newer-discovery item — 1) D 2) D (second line) 3) G 4) R … A) Decreased dopamine activity B) Decreased vitamin-D level C) Hypogonadism with decreased testosterone D) Renin–aldosterone-system activation
items.exp: The Dirty dozen lines list decreased dopamine activity, decreased vitamin-D level, hypogonadism with decreased testosterone, and renin–aldosterone-system activation. (Book p919)

items.q: The 'Treacherous 13' adds serotonin, which increases hormone-sensitive ___.
items.exp: The Treacherous 13 line reads dirty dozen plus serotonin leading to increased hormone-sensitive lipase. (Book p919)

items.q: Assess the three mnemonic lines: I Treacherous 13 is Dirty dozen plus serotonin. II Faithless 14 adds iron in the beta-cell.
items.exp: The page explicitly defines Treacherous 13 as Dirty dozen plus serotonin and Faithless 14 as Treacherous 13 plus iron in the beta-cell. (Book p919)

items.q: In the final mnemonic, iron in the beta-cell is associated on the page with:
items.exp: Faithless 14 is annotated as iron in the beta-cell causing toxicity and resistance. (Book p919)

items.q: How many of the four diagnostic criteria does the page require for diabetes in its flowchart?
items.exp: The diabetes flowchart places '≥1 out of 4' over the four diagnostic branches. (Book p919)

items.q: Match the diagnostic branch to its printed cut-off — 1) HbA1c 2) Fasting plasma glucose 3) 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose 4) RBS with symptoms … A) ≥6.5% B) ≥126 mg/dL C) 75-g glucose ≥200 mg/dL D) ≥200 mg/dL
items.exp: The four branches are HbA1c ≥6.5%, fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL, 2-hour postprandial glucose after 75-g glucose ≥200 mg/dL, and RBS ≥200 mg/dL with clinical symptoms. (Book p919)

items.q: An RBS value reaches the threshold on this page and the patient has the listed classic symptoms. Which action is supported by the flowchart?
opts: Recognize diabetes using RBS ≥200 mg/dL plus clinical symptoms
items.exp: The page's fourth branch pairs RBS ≥200 mg/dL with clinical symptoms for the diabetes diagnosis. (Book p919)

items.q: Assess the symptom arrows: I Hyperosmotic glucose draws water from the cell. II The page links weight loss with decreased effective-volume depletion.
items.exp: The page links increased glucose to hyperosmotic water movement from cells and links weight loss to decreased effective volume depletion and increased catabolic effect. (Book p919)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the classic symptoms written beside the RBS branch?
items.exp: Polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss are listed beside the RBS branch; hemoptysis is not. (Book p919)

items.q: The page states that what percentage of patients become diabetic every year in the pre-diabetes section?
items.exp: The pre-diabetes heading is followed by the statement that 10–15% of patients become diabetic every year. (Book p919)

items.q: Match the table row to the pre-diabetes range — 1) Fasting value 2) 2-hour PPBG (75 g) 3) HbA1c values … A) 100–125 mg/dL B) 140–199 mg/dL C) 5.7–6.4%
items.exp: The pre-diabetes table gives fasting 100–125 mg/dL, 2-hour PPBG 140–199 mg/dL and HbA1c 5.7–6.4%. (Book p919)

items.q: The normal 2-hour PPBG value in the table is less than ___ mg/dL.
items.exp: The normal-value column lists 2-hour PPBG (75 g) as <140 mg/dL. (Book p919)
